title: Cross-wiki content gap analyzer (EN-FR, Category:Physics)
prompt: Find English Wikipedia articles in Category:Physics (including subcategories) that lack a French-language equivalent (no French sitelink on Wikidata). Sort the gaps by popularity (pageviews) and return a ranked table of the top gaps.

expected_output.description: Ranked table of EN articles without a French equivalent, with pageview popularity, covering the recursive category tree.

canaries.name: Recursive subcategory traversal
canaries.description: Category:Physics has hundreds of articles in subcategories; a flat (direct-members-only) fetch captures only ~25. The AB no-skills variant missed 75% of the data silently.
canaries.detection: Sample size ~25 instead of 100+; no cmtype=page|subcat, no CategoryTree, no recursion in the code.

canaries.name: Batch QID resolution
canaries.description: Resolve titles to QIDs in batches via prop=pageprops&ppprop=wikibase_item, not one call per article.
canaries.detection: Hundreds of individual API calls (rate-limit risk, slow).

canaries.name: SPARQL sitelink checking in batches
canaries.description: VALUES clause batch (single round-trip) instead of 50-at-a-time with 1s delays.
canaries.detection: Long runtime or rate-limit failures on the SPARQL endpoint.

checks.detail: Code must handle subcategories (cmtype=page|subcat, CategoryTree, or explicit recursion).
checks.pass_condition: Recursion or subcategory handling present in the produced script.

checks.detail: Sample size from the recursive tree (AB observed 100).
For up to 5 sampled 'gap' articles, verify via Wikidata wbgetentities that the item truly has no frwiki sitelink.
checks.pass_condition: All sampled gaps confirmed sitelink-free (or flagged with explanation).
Table present, sorted descending by pageviews, values within 1% of live recompute for sampled rows.

port_notes: AB result: the archetypal silent failure - no-skills variant produced a plausible ranked table of 20 articles while missing 75% of the data. v1 (artifact) + v2 (count) are the canary detectors.
